title: Episode 118: C++ Allocators with Zach Laine! (Part 2)

sentences.en: Wait, weren't you a ninth grader?
sentences.zh: 等等，你不是九年级的学生吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think of like, you know, a young kid wants to cut up frogs.
sentences.zh: 我想到的是，你知道，那种想解剖青蛙的小屁孩。

sentences.en: I'm thinking like eight.
sentences.zh: 我觉得大概八岁左右吧。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast episode 118, recorded on February 16th, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 118 期，录制于 2023 年 2 月 16 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we interview Zach Lane.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起采访 Zach Lane。

sentences.en: This is part two of a probably four-part interview series.
sentences.zh: 这是四部分采访系列的第二部分。

sentences.en: If you missed part one, check the link in the description for episode 117.
sentences.zh: 如果你错过了第一部分，请查看第 117 期的描述链接。

sentences.en: We talk about C++ allocators and lots more.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了 C++ 分配器以及更多内容。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of strong opinions that you hold, you are, I think, famously one of the people on the committee who has very low tolerance for allocators.
sentences.zh: 说到你持有的强烈观点，我想你作为委员会成员之一，以对分配器的容忍度极低而闻名。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: What do you have against allocators?
sentences.zh: 你对分配器有什么意见？

sentences.en: I want to create a scenario in which allocators are just asleep in their bed, and then they smell smoke, and the allocators try to get out of the house, but I've locked them all
sentences.zh: 我想创造一个场景，让分配器们正躺在床上睡觉，然后闻到了烟味，它们试图逃出房子，但我已经从外面把它们锁上了，

sentences.en: with padlocks from the outside.
sentences.zh: 用挂锁锁住。

sentences.en: The allocators die and fire.
sentences.zh: 分配器们在火中丧生。

sentences.en: That's what I want.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想要的。

sentences.en: I'm not going to say they should die slowly.
sentences.zh: 我不是说它们应该死得很慢。

sentences.en: I want it to be quick, but I want it to be painful.
sentences.zh: 我希望它发生得很快，但我希望它很痛苦。

sentences.en: I just don't like allocators.
sentences.zh: 我就是不喜欢分配器。

sentences.en: I hate them.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌它们。

sentences.en: So to me, the killer argument against allocators is just think of vector, like the simplest type that we have that allocates memory, right?
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，反对分配器的致命论点就是想想 vector，比如我们拥有的最简单的分配内存的类型，对吧？

sentences.en: So a vector at a high-level abstraction, a vector is a thing that manages the storage of heap-allocated buffer of stuff, okay?
sentences.zh: 所以从高层抽象来看，vector 是一个管理堆分配缓冲区存储的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Heap-allocated array of T.
sentences.zh: T 类型的堆分配数组。

sentences.en: And you can, or this is not actually allowed with the typical allocator.
sentences.zh: 你可以，或者说这在典型的分配器中实际上是不允许的。

sentences.en: People have tried to change the allocator model so that you can do this.
sentences.zh: 人们试图改变分配器模型，以便你可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: And the this I'm thinking of is make it where you can substitute in an allocator, and basically you get a small vector, right?
sentences.zh: 我所想的“这一点”是，让你能够替换一个分配器，基本上你得到一个小型 vector，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it's got a small buffer optimization, and then it goes to the heap.
sentences.zh: 就像它有一个小型缓冲区优化，然后它才去堆上分配。

sentences.en: Or worse yet, you just drop in an allocator, and now it's a static vector.
sentences.zh: 或者更糟的是，你直接放入一个分配器，现在它变成了一个静态 vector。

sentences.en: So all of its allocations happen in a fixed-size buffer.
sentences.zh: 所以它所有的分配都发生在固定大小的缓冲区中。

sentences.en: If you exceed that, it's either UB or you get an exception.
sentences.zh: 如果你超过了这个大小，要么是未定义行为 (UB)，要么你会得到一个异常。

sentences.en: There's different schools of thought on what to do there, but the idea is it never allocates, right?
sentences.zh: 关于那里该怎么做有不同的学派，但想法是它永远不会分配，对吧？

sentences.en: But it gives the same vector interface, right?
sentences.zh: 但它提供了相同的 vector 接口，对吧？

sentences.en: That's incredibly useful.
sentences.zh: 这非常有用。

sentences.en: The problem is when you do it with an allocator, you've already lost before you've started.
sentences.zh: 问题在于当你用分配器来做这件事时，你还没开始就已经输了。

sentences.en: And the reason is that if you implement vector, you will find that the way you do things when you reallocate is completely different based on whether you may or may not be going to
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果你实现 vector，你会发现你重新分配时做事的方式，完全取决于你是否可能去

sentences.en: the heap.
sentences.zh: 堆上分配。

sentences.en: You never go to the heap, or you always go to the heap.
sentences.zh: 你从不去堆上，或者你总是去堆上。

sentences.en: So adding a new element, the code looks completely different when you have to resize the array, right?
sentences.zh: 所以添加一个新元素时，当你必须调整数组大小时，代码看起来完全不同，对吧？

sentences.en: And the problem with that is that if you just substitute in the allocator, you cannot make the code change in something like pushback or insert.
sentences.zh: 而这带来的问题是，如果你只是替换了分配器，你无法在 pushback 或 insert 之类的地方改变代码。

sentences.en: It's fixed.
sentences.zh: 它是固定的。

sentences.en: It only works a certain way.
sentences.zh: 它只能以某种方式工作。

sentences.en: Now, what you could do is you could write the vector where it knows about all these possible
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以做的是编写 vector，让它了解所有这些可能的

sentences.en: styles of allocation, appreciates them as alternatives, and there's some kind of static thing about
sentences.zh: 分配风格，将它们视为替代方案，并且关于

sentences.en: the allocator model where it can detect, oh, I'm a thing that never allocates, or I'm a thing
sentences.zh: 分配器模型有一些静态的东西，它可以检测到，哦，我是一个从不分配的东西，或者我是一个

sentences.en: that always allocates, or I'm a thing that might allocate, and then you could have this really complicated code for what vector does.
sentences.zh: 总是分配的东西，或者我是一个可能会分配的东西，然后你可以为 vector 的行为编写这种非常复杂的代码。

sentences.en: I think a better alternative is to say we have three flavors of vector.
sentences.zh: 我认为更好的选择是说我们有三种风格的 vector。

sentences.en: We have the three flavors that do those things, and they never deal with an allocator.
sentences.zh: 我们有做那些事情的三种风格，它们从不处理分配器。

sentences.en: And if you want the old allocator stuff, you std vector, and we have the std2 vector that does the right thing, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你想要旧的分配器东西，就用 std vector，我们有做正确事情的 std2 vector，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is it just allocates.
sentences.zh: 也就是它直接分配。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Boom.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: Uses new, right?
sentences.zh: 使用 new，对吧？

sentences.en: Heresy, but that's what it does.
sentences.zh: 异端邪说，但它就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And then we have another one that's a static vector, and it just works with a buffer.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有另一个是静态 vector，它只使用缓冲区工作。

sentences.en: And then another one's a small vector.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个是小型 vector。

sentences.en: And I think if we had a good story for people writing a std vector for a std vector compatible
sentences.zh: 我认为如果我们为人们编写一个 std vector 兼容的

sentences.en: thing of their own, then we would have a good story for standardizing such a thing, because we'd have a small interface, and you could just standardize a small interface, and it's
sentences.zh: 东西有一个好的方案，那么我们就会有一个好的标准化方案，因为我们有一个小接口，你可以直接标准化一个小接口，而且

sentences.en: not much work to standardize, just like it's not much work to write it as an end user.
sentences.zh: 标准化它不需要太多工作，就像作为最终用户编写它不需要太多工作一样。

sentences.en: I think that is the much, much better answer.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是更好、更好的答案。

sentences.en: But the big problem that I have with allocators, the thing that started getting me so dead set
sentences.zh: 但我对分配器最大的问题，让我开始如此坚决地

sentences.en: against them was when I heard that we added all these constructors to the container adapters.
sentences.zh: 反对它们的事情是，当我听说我们给容器适配器添加了所有这些构造函数时。

sentences.en: And for those of you who don't know, container adapter is something that takes an existing container and just provides some semantics on it.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人，容器适配器是获取现有容器并为其提供一些语义的东西。

sentences.en: So std stack takes, by default, a vector, but you can always use a deck, any random access thing, anything that grows at the end efficiently.
sentences.zh: 所以 std stack 默认使用 vector，但你总是可以使用 deque，任何随机访问的东西，任何在末尾高效增长的东西。

sentences.en: So you can push back, push back, push back, pop back, pop back, pop back, and then it acts as a stack, okay?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以 push back，push back，push back，pop back，pop back，pop back，然后它就作为栈运行，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, under the covers, it's just a vector, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，在底层，它只是一个 vector，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you have a vector that has a custom allocator, which is part of the vectors type, that's the way allocators work, you could just stick that into your stack.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个带有自定义分配器的 vector，这是 vector 类型的一部分，分配器就是这样工作的，你可以直接把它塞进你的栈里。

sentences.en: Like, there's no need for the stack to know about allocation or allocators.
sentences.zh: 就像，栈根本不需要知道分配或分配器。

sentences.en: It doesn't allocate, right?
sentences.zh: 它不分配，对吧？

sentences.en: It just forwards through operations and the length thing, but it has all these constructor parameters that are optional for allocators.
sentences.zh: 它只是转发操作和长度之类的东西，但它有所有这些可选的分配器构造函数参数。

sentences.en: So we're polluting these non-allocating things with allocator parameters.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在用分配器参数污染这些不分配的东西。

sentences.en: Worse yet, we've done the same thing with tuple and pair and now optional.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，我们在 tuple、pair 和现在的 optional 上也做了同样的事情。

sentences.en: People are trying.
sentences.zh: 人们正在尝试。

sentences.en: All these other things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些其他东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: People are trying to add all these interfaces that do this allocating stuff to things that never allocate.
sentences.zh: 人们正试图将所有这些执行分配操作的接口添加到从不分配的东西上。

sentences.en: And that makes me crazy, like, because there's a non-trivial cost to all these things.
sentences.zh: 这让我发疯，因为所有这些东西都有不小的成本。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: So what are these extra constructors that are customized by allocators doing?
sentences.zh: 那么这些由分配器定制的额外构造函数在做什么？

sentences.en: I missed that part.
sentences.zh: 我错过了那部分。

sentences.en: That's one of the costs.
sentences.zh: 那是成本之一。

sentences.en: Explaining it to people.
sentences.zh: 向人们解释它。

sentences.en: Teachability is hard, right?
sentences.zh: 可教性很难，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not kidding.
sentences.zh: 我没开玩笑。

sentences.en: That's like, really, like, what is that doing?
sentences.zh: 那就像，真的，那到底在做什么？

sentences.en: I don't understand that interface.
sentences.zh: 我不理解那个接口。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So what it's doing is there is a notion in the library part of the standard of uses allocator construction, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它在做的是，在标准库部分有一个“使用分配器构造”的概念，对吧？

sentences.en: So all of those things do uses allocator construction on the vector that you pass in, like in the stack case, right?
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些东西都对你传入的 vector 执行“使用分配器构造”，比如在 stack 的情况下，对吧？

sentences.en: You construct it with a vector, let's say.
sentences.zh: 你用一个 vector 构造它，比方说。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And then you provide an allocator, and it uses that allocator, not the one that comes with
sentences.zh: 然后你提供一个分配器，它使用那个分配器，而不是随

sentences.en: the vector, and it does uses allocator construction to do the allocation for constructing that vector.
sentences.zh: vector 一起提供的那个，它执行“使用分配器构造”来为构造那个 vector 进行分配。

sentences.en: Sometimes you might also use the, there's another interface, like just basically the default constructor, you can pass an allocator parameter.
sentences.zh: 有时你可能也会使用，还有另一个接口，基本上就是默认构造函数，你可以传递一个分配器参数。

sentences.en: So like it's now a unary constructor instead of the default constructor.
sentences.zh: 所以它现在是一个一元构造函数，而不是默认构造函数。

sentences.en: And it, again, does uses allocator construction, except you're not even passing it a vector, you're using the one inside, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它再次执行“使用分配器构造”，只是你甚至没有传递一个 vector，你使用的是内部的那个，对吧？

sentences.en: So this all begs the question, like, why do we need any of these things?
sentences.zh: 所以这一切引出了一个问题，我们为什么需要这些东西中的任何一个？

sentences.en: I can just take an existing vector, move it into there, and then I've got the uses allocator construction because I did the allocator construction on the side of it.
sentences.zh: 我可以只取一个现有的 vector，移动到那里，然后我就有了“使用分配器构造”，因为我在它旁边做了分配器构造。

sentences.en: Why are we, why don't we have separation of concerns here?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们，为什么我们这里没有关注点分离？

sentences.en: The answer is, it is a mystery.
sentences.zh: 答案是，这是一个谜。

sentences.en: Like, I've never been able to get a straight answer about why we add those things to those.
sentences.zh: 我从来没能得到一个直接的答案，关于为什么我们要把那些东西加到这些东西上。

sentences.en: But the reason for adding them to things like tuple is that, again, the tuple might contain something like a string, and so it needs to know about uses allocator construction, and
sentences.zh: 但把它们加到像 tuple 这样的东西上的原因是，同样，tuple 可能包含像 string 这样的东西，所以它需要了解“使用分配器构造”，

sentences.en: so it needs to be allocator aware is the term of art that the allocator folks use.
sentences.zh: 所以它需要是“分配器感知”的，这是分配器相关人员使用的术语。

sentences.en: So I find that to be anathema, that something that doesn't allocate has to allocate.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现这简直是令人厌恶，一个不分配的东西竟然必须分配。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is, you know, I have mixed feelings about allocators.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我对分配器有复杂的情绪。

sentences.en: I have very strong opposition to the uses allocator pattern and its viral nature across, you know, vocabulary types that do not allocate.
sentences.zh: 我非常强烈地反对“使用分配器”模式及其在不分配的词汇类型中的病毒式传播。

sentences.en: But so, okay, so your argument for why we shouldn't want allocators in vector, I actually buy that,
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，关于为什么我们不应该在 vector 中想要分配器的论点，我实际上是认同的，

sentences.en: that I think that something like a, you know, a small vector, a stack vector should be a separate type.
sentences.zh: 我认为像小型 vector、栈 vector 这样的东西应该是一个单独的类型。

sentences.en: But what if I just like, you know, I have my own, like, memory pool that I want to, you know,
sentences.zh: 但如果我只是，你知道，我有我自己的内存池，我想，你知道，

sentences.en: stick into vector, or if I want to have a vector that, you know, is backed by some special memory, like GPU memory or some fast memory that's available in my system.
sentences.zh: 塞进 vector，或者如果我想拥有一个由特殊内存支持的 vector，比如 GPU 内存或我系统中可用的某种快速内存。

sentences.en: Why should I have to write my own vector for that?
sentences.zh: 为什么我必须为此编写我自己的 vector？

sentences.en: So this is a classic example of asking the wrong question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个问错问题的经典例子。

sentences.en: You've asked a question that has an obvious answer, but the answer feels obvious because the question is wrong.
sentences.zh: 你问了一个有明显答案的问题，但这个答案之所以感觉明显，是因为问题本身是错的。

sentences.en: So I think you should turn around and say it this way.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你应该换个角度说。

sentences.en: We know that the number of template instantiations of std vector that contain an allocator template parameter is less than a percent of a percent, right?
sentences.zh: 我们知道包含分配器模板参数的 std vector 的模板实例化数量不到百分之一的百分之一，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, just the total number of instantiations in the world in user code is somewhere.
sentences.zh: 就像，用户代码中全世界实例化的总数在某个地方。

sentences.en: Let's be gratuitous and say it's about a percent.
sentences.zh: 我们慷慨一点，说它大约是百分之一。

sentences.en: So the real question is why should that 99% of users have to deal with allocators to support that 1% of users, right?
sentences.zh: 所以真正的问题是，为什么那 99% 的用户必须为了支持那 1% 的用户而处理分配器，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we want the standard library to be, like, useful tools that everybody can make use out of,
sentences.zh: 我们希望标准库是每个人都能利用的有用工具，

sentences.en: and if there's some squirrely edge cases, then you write your own squirrely edge case code.
sentences.zh: 如果有一些古怪的边缘情况，那么你就编写你自己的古怪边缘情况代码。

sentences.en: But here's the crazy part.
sentences.zh: 但疯狂的部分在这里。

sentences.en: Like, people are doing exactly what you said.
sentences.zh: 人们正在做你说的完全一样的事情。

sentences.en: They're making pool allocators, and they're using with vector, and they're getting great results out of it, and that's fine.
sentences.zh: 他们正在制作池分配器，并与 vector 一起使用，他们从中获得了很好的结果，这很好。

sentences.en: We already have that.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有了那个。

sentences.en: Like, we don't need, like, if you want to use a vector with an allocator, hey, go crazy.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不需要，如果你想用分配器使用 vector，嘿，尽管去用吧。

sentences.en: Like, we support that already, right?
sentences.zh: 我们已经支持了，对吧？

sentences.en: There's another, so we can just keep the existing code and just not write any new allocator-led stuff,
sentences.zh: 还有另一个，所以我们可以保留现有的代码，只是不编写任何新的分配器主导的东西，

sentences.en: and we've covered most of the people that are doing exactly the use case you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们就覆盖了大多数正在做你所说的用例的人。

sentences.en: Then we've got other people like, you know, EA and Bloomberg, where, like, they've re-implemented the SDL, and they've re-implemented all their own allocators,
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有其他人，比如 EA 和 Bloomberg，他们重新实现了 SDL，他们重新实现了他们自己所有的分配器，

sentences.en: and they don't actually need the standard stuff because they do their own thing.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上不需要标准的东西，因为他们做他们自己的事情。

sentences.en: And so the allocator model has been adopted by lots of organizations that don't even use the actual, like, code from the standard library because they really like this model.
sentences.zh: 所以分配器模型已经被许多组织采用，他们甚至不使用标准库中的实际代码，因为他们真的很喜欢这个模型。

sentences.en: And wherever they find something like, well, I'm allocating with an allocator here, but then the value type doesn't use an allocator.
sentences.zh: 无论他们发现什么，比如，好吧，我在这里用分配器分配，但值类型不使用分配器。

sentences.en: I need to be able to pass all that through.
sentences.zh: 我需要能够传递所有这些。

sentences.en: They want allocators all the way down.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一直到底的分配器。

sentences.en: And so they have to have a different organization to their code than what is provided in the standard library.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的代码组织方式必须与标准库中提供的不同。

sentences.en: And so, you know, to those people, I say go crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以，对那些人，我说尽管去吧。

sentences.en: Do your thing, right?
sentences.zh: 做你们的事，对吧？

sentences.en: But don't make everyone else drag that stuff around because you're making use out of it because you are in the 1% case.
